title: Accelerator tiling weekly surface snapshot - per-pool slot packing (2026-09-05)
body:
Summary:
This sheet is an export from the weekly utilization surface (tiling+packing view) focused on how the tile allocator changed apparent pool-level occupancy across clusters and regions for 2026-08-30 -> 2026-09-05.

Key takeaway:
- Tiling enabled denser small-request packing on tensor nodes, improving effective utilization on 'latency' pools by ~9% on average while keeping p95 tail latency within SLO for short sequences.
- A sustained fragmentation issue observed on cluster-aurora/reserved pool (stale 1h reservations) — recoverable via reservation TTL enforcement (see action items).

Per-cluster / per-pool weekly snapshot (daily columns show avg utilization %):
Cluster | Pool       | Region | 2026-08-30 | 2026-08-31 | 2026-09-01 | 2026-09-02 | 2026-09-03 | 2026-09-04 | 2026-09-05 | avg_seq_len | microburst_count | p95_ms | slot_frag_pct
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

phi-01  | batch      | us-west| 48         | 46         | 52         | 50         | 47         | 49         | 51         | 120         | 6                | 220   | 6

sable   | reserved   | apac   | 70         | 69         | 71         | 72         | 73         | 74         | 75         | 300         | 0                | 430   | 20

Observations / anomalies:
- aurora/reserved slot_frag_pct spikes to 72% on 2026-09-05 (highest across fleet). Correlates with a backlog of stale 1h reservations created by failed teardown job INFRA-3284 on 2026-09-04 23:00 UTC.
- phi-01 shows highest microburst_count in latency pool (14) and modest p95 improvements post-tiling rollout (p95 reduced ~6ms vs pre-tiling baseline measured two weeks prior).
- batch pools across regions are stable but show slightly higher avg_seq_len on weekend days; suggests a different job mix on peak batch windows.

Quick metrics notes (how surface calculates fields):
- utilization % = occupied VRAM / total VRAM capacity per pool, averaged over 5m windows across each day.
- microburst_count = # of 1s windows with >2x baseline token throughput (tiling can change baseline).
- slot_frag_pct = fraction of allocated slots with <25% VRAM used (indicates fragmentation).

Suggested immediate actions:
1) Reservation TTL enforcement: backfill small script to sweep stale reservations and issue soft-termination (owner: Marco, ticket INFRA-3284).
2) Temporarily increase reserved-pool reclamation aggressiveness on aurora by lowering soft-ttl to 20m for new reservations for 24h (A/B measure).
3) Run tiling backfill sim for eu region with current request mix to validate packing heuristics for reserved-heavy workloads (owner: Priya).
4) Add p95-by-seq-length curve to the surface export so we can see whether tail regression is sequence-length-specific (tracking: github PR 72).

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Weekly rerun: 2026-09-12 snapshot post-reclamation.
- Ops playbook note: add 'stale reservation' troubleshooting section to Confluence playbook (confluence://infra/accelerator-tiling-playbook).

Notes to self / open questions (working doc style):
- Are there reservation patterns caused by specific customers or query types? Need customer-annotated logs (privacy-sanitized).
- Consider brief experiment: enable compact-tiling for latency pool only during 00:00-06:00 UTC to chase lower cost for trailing EU traffic.

Raw export attached (CSV view):
- file: accelerator_tiling_surface_export_2026-09-05.csv (S3: s3://redwood-exports/infra/accelerator_tiling/2026-09-05.csv)

End of snapshot.
